findings.title: The sudoers rules grant unrestricted root execution through operator-controlled commands
findings.description: The `MT_RUN` wildcard allows `manta` to invoke `/usr/local/bin/mt-run` with arbitrary arguments as root, including its pass-through to the production `mt` CLI. More critically, `MT_INSTALL` runs the installer from the operator’s checkout under `/home/manta`; if that checkout is writable by `manta`, the operator can modify the script and execute arbitrary code as root. These rules exceed the stated limited-command scope and provide a privilege-escalation path. Restrict the permitted arguments and ensure any root-executed script is root-owned and not operator-writable.

findings.title: The bounded firing still blocks until the entire minute pass ends
findings.description: `run(["mt-run", *mt_run_args], ..., stream=True)` is synchronous. The installed `mt-run minute` starts the systemd unit and then waits for it to finish before exiting, so `wait_for_unit_or_line()` is not reached when the trailing-complete journal line appears. The cutover therefore still waits through unbounded backfill instead of stopping the unit after trailing work. Start the unit without blocking (for example, via `systemctl start --no-block`) and monitor its journal independently. The current tests mock `run` to return immediately, so they do not cover this behavior.

findings.title: A timestamp-valid but unusable bar can falsely complete a session
findings.description: Session judgement counts any bar with a parseable timestamp, but `_insert_minute_bars` later skips bars with missing, non-numeric, non-finite, or non-positive OHLC values. If a response contains only such bars during a session, `judge_chunk_by_sessions()` can mark the chunk `SUCCESS` and gap advancement can delete its row even though no usable session bars were stored. Judge only bars that pass the same validity rules as insertion, or share a validation/conversion step so accounting matches what is persisted.
